the_movies_blueprint:
The Movies is the direct ancestor and its core teaching machinery is exactly what Project: Studio is missing. What it got right, and we must match: (1) The film is ONE physical token that travels the lot — script page at the Script Office, camera icon during shooting, film can at release — and its HUD card icon always matches its physical location. Players learned the pipeline by carrying the same object through buildings in order. (2) Buildings are verb menus: click a building, walls drop, and the floorplan exposes named drop rooms ('Begin Casting', 'Shoot It', 'Release'). The Casting Office floorplan doubles as the production checklist — every unfilled role is a visibly empty room. (3) One universal gesture (pick-up/drop to act, right-click/hover to inspect) taught in minute one at the Gate's visible hiring queue and never replaced. (4) Guiding Streams: pick up anything and a sparkling trail draws to the most sensible drop target — ignorable, suggestive, with Tab jumping to the highest-priority pending action, and streams even highlighting missing buildings in the Build menu. (5) Imperative stage-completion bubbles ('Your script is complete and ready for casting in the Casting Office') that name the building and the verb, never just a stat. (6) Structural sequencing: 1920 era-gating meant the first film needed 1-2 actors, one set, and advanced buildings literally didn't exist yet; the tutorial spawned a free finished script at the gates so film #1 starts at casting, the most tactile stage. (7) Traceable judgment: hover a critic's comment to see which factor caused it; a free test screening via the Reviews room. (8) Layered attention: priority-sorted info bubbles with threshold ticks, red/green pips, the PA announcer, timeline icons — with a player-adjustable help level.

What it got wrong, and we must beat: (1) Two games taped together — the machinima toolset ran parallel to the tycoon sim; hand-crafted films had no economic meaning. Our watching-the-production layer must stay a consequence-viewer of package decisions, never a separate creative suite. (2) Nanny micromanagement killed it: literally re-dragging stars together to build friendships, chasing them out of the bar, repeated identical drags with no delegation ramp. Any repeated care action must graduate to policy/delegates. (3) Bubble clutter at scale — the prioritization that worked early drowned in a big studio; we must cap simultaneous surfaces and route repeats into a ticker. (4) Opaque quality formula: nine hidden factors, with fan wikis existing to reverse-engineer it; every review line must decompose on hover into package decisions. (5) No failure drama: 'a disastrous shoot that over-runs... is just never going to happen,' so bigger-is-better flattened greenlighting into churn. (6) Gameable prestige (dotting trees/expensive cars) — any lot-quality number must be causal and legible or cut. (7) Real-time pressure taxed deliberate play — our deterministic weekly tick is the fix, provided reading the lot never costs the player anything. The remake thesis: keep the token, the rooms, the streams, and the imperative bubbles; replace the nannying with delegation, the opacity with decomposable causes, and the parallel auteur toy with a single integrated tycoon loop.

A_guidance_layer: Model it on Two Point Hospital's star-objectives panel, not a tutorial: a persistent, collapsible checklist whose steps ARE the filmmaking chain ('Commission a screenplay' -> 'Review the draft' -> 'Run auditions' -> 'Assemble the package' -> 'Greenlight' -> 'Watch Week 1 of shooting' -> 'Release'). Each step ticks only when its physical consequence appears on the lot (writer at desk, actors queuing, cast walking to stage) — derive every step from engine state, never from a scripted flag.

Every guidance line is written imperatively in The Movies' bubble voice — building + verb: 'Your screenplay is ready for review at Development & Casting,' never 'Script: complete.' Subject + place + problem/next-verb in one sentence (Zoo Tycoon's 'Snow Leopard 1 has escaped into Exhibit 1' grammar).

Clicking a guidance step PANS the camera across the lot to the relevant building/person (the pans-not-teleports ruling) — this is RCT's click-the-ticker-to-jump rule plus The Movies' Tab-to-highest-priority-stream, softened into a pan so the player learns lot geography en route.

When the next step is blocked, the guidance layer must name the blocking dependency and make it clickable ('Auditions cannot start: no screenplay approved — review the draft at Development & Casting'). This directly fixes RCT's most-complained-about hole: the silent 'is still broken down' loop where the cause (no path to the exit) was never messaged.

Include a pull-based advisor verb alongside the push checklist: a Unit Production Manager / studio fixer button on the studio (Zoo Tycoon's zookeeper-recommendations panel) that converts current state into a shopping list in the exact vocabulary of the player's verbs. The advice vocabulary and the button labels on buildings must be identical strings — ZT works because 'needs more foliage' maps 1:1 onto the foliage tab.

Collapse gracefully: after the first film releases, the layer shrinks to a one-line 'next best action' ticker entry rather than a full checklist; The Movies' adjustable 'Level of Help Provided' option is the precedent for making guidance density player-tunable.
B_building_hierarchy: Level 1 (what is this): hover/first-click gives a same-shaped card for EVERY building — name, function in one sentence, occupants count. Zoo Tycoon's rule: because every panel rhymes, learning one teaches all; actor/writer/building/production cards must share one skeleton (portrait, name, 3-5 meters, one advice/action button).

Level 2 (what is happening): an Anno 1800-style status icon floats over every building at all times — Soundstage: 'no production assigned' / 'awaiting cast' / 'rehearsing, week 3 of 6' / 'stalled: no director'; Development: quill icon with draft progress. Every weekly-tick stall names its cause above the building where it stalled, readable at camera range before any panel opens.

Level 3 (what can I do now): opening the building lowers its roof into The Movies' floorplan-as-verb-menu — Development & Casting exposes a Commission Desk, Readers' Room, Audition Stage, and a Packaging Table with visibly empty director/cast/budget slots. Available verbs light up; unavailable verbs are visible but grayed with the unmet condition named (Two Point Hospital's required-items checklist: nothing activates while a requirement is unmet, and the unmet item is named).

Level 4 (deep details): the tabbed dossier, modeled on RCT's ride window — one persistent, non-modal window per building with icon-tab lenses (View/live activity, Assignments, History, Finances). Panels are read-mostly and always second handles on the lot object: every row that references a person or production is a click-to-pan link back into the world (The Movies' right-click-a-build-menu-item-zooms-to-the-facility rule).

When a package becomes greenlightable, the building itself announces the verb: Anno's residence upgrade arrow translated to 1948 — a klieg-light beam sprouts from Development & Casting. The building advertises the next step; the player never hunts menus.

Never let a panel complete an action the building can't show. The Owner's complaint ('the chain is hidden in management panels') is precisely The Movies' inverse rule violated: panels are dossiers and handles, buildings are where verbs live.
C_film_world_object: The film is ONE named, persistent, followable token from commission to release, auto-named ('Untitled Western No. 1', renameable in one click, per RCT's ride naming), whose icon morphs per phase: script binder -> production slate -> camera -> film cans -> premiere marquee. The Movies proved the icon-matches-location trick is how players learn the chain without reading.

Anchor it to a place every week: the token renders at its current phase's building each tick — a card on the soundstage door reading 'Stage 2 — DESERT SERENADE — SHOOTING, week 3 of 6' (Zoo Tycoon's exhibit-as-named-world-object). Clicking the stage and clicking the production card open the same window; panel and place are one object.

Phase transitions are watchable physical events (Zoo Tycoon 2's crates, Parkitect's carried goods): commissioning puts a writer visibly typing at Development with pages piling up; the finished draft is walked to Administration by a courier; greenlighting sends the cast and crew walking from Development & Casting to the soundstage; post sends film cans carried to the lab; release stages a premiere at the Gate. The weekly tick animates that week's happenings — presence IS the progress bar.

Give the production an RCT ride-window dossier with tabbed lenses: View (live camera on wherever it physically is), Package (script/director/cast/budget slots), Schedule (phase, weeks remaining), Costs, and later Audience (aggregated reactions). It accrues lifetime history — grosses, reviews, awards — the way a coaster accrues lifetime customers.

The production card on the screen edge is a second handle, The Movies-style: click to pan the camera to the token; every alert about the film references it by name and place ('DESERT SERENADE has stalled in Rehearsal — no leading lady, Stage 2').

The package assembly board shows a live viability meter that moves as slots fill (Zoo Tycoon's suitability bar climbing while you paint terrain, Planet Zoo's live red/green requirement bars during habitat editing) — greenlight readiness is tuned by watching a needle, not by knowing a rule. The Greenlight button is Two Point Hospital's green checkmark: disabled with the missing slot named until the checklist completes.
D_attention_language: Three channels, three tempos, all diegetic and 1948-flavored: a trade-paper/PA news ticker for events (RCT's attention spine — every message has an icon, a period-appropriate sound, and a lot address; clicking pans there; a Recent Messages archive exists); floating status icons over buildings for standing state (Anno); mood/state glyphs worn on people for individual state (Zoo Tycoon's smiley/frowny faces, Two Point Hospital's illnesses-as-costumes: idle contract player lounging by the Gate, star carrying sides during rehearsal, unhappy director pacing).

No mobile-game flashing: attention escalates by physicality first, then text. The lot should look wrong before any number does (Parkitect's out-of-stock signs and trash, TPH's queues spilling into corridors) — a dark cobwebbed soundstage says 'wasted capacity,' idle contract players playing cards say 'payroll burning.'

The Guiding Stream, restrained: when the player selects/holds an actionable object, draw one tasteful trail (dust-mote sparkle, searchlight sweep) to the most sensible target, explicitly ignorable, exactly as The Movies' manual framed it ('this is only a suggestion'). Never more than one stream at once.

Bubbles are hover-triggered and priority-sorted with visible threshold ticks (The Movies), pull-based where possible (Zoo Tycoon's advisor waits to be asked) — and hard rate-limited: cap simultaneous bubbles, collapse repeats into one ticker line, aggregate patterns into a chorus message ('Exhibitors complain you have released nothing this quarter') instead of per-entity spam. Both The Movies and ZT2 documented the drowning failure.
Overlays are opt-in lenses only, one key, never auto-popping (Planet Zoo's whiteout heatmap complaints): at most one or two view modes (e.g., Morale tint on people, Buzz tint on productions).

If a voice exists, it is TPH's model — a lot loudspeaker delivering short diegetic status lines as ambient telemetry ('Stage 3 is dark again') with an adjustable assistance level (The Movies' PA option) — never instruction, never chatty (Planet Zoo's muted-and-resented narrators).

Every judgment decomposes on hover: review lines, box-office results, and any derived score must click through to named causes (The Movies' hoverable critic comments; the anti-lesson is ZT1's unexplainable 0-star popularity wall).
E_golden_path: Pre-complete the slowest step: start the 1948 studio with one commissioned screenplay already delivered and waiting at Development & Casting (The Movies' free script at the gates), so session one runs review -> audition -> package -> greenlight -> shoot -> release, and commissioning becomes film #2's lesson. Cast-first onboarding beats commission-first onboarding.

Constrain the first decision space structurally, not with tutorial text (The Movies' 1920 era-gating, ZT1's tiny starter adoption list): film #1 is a one-lead B-picture — one screenplay, one available director, two or three audition candidates, one open soundstage. Gate Publicity spend, prestige packaging, and multi-stage epics behind a readable reputation milestone (The Movies' certificate ranks with explicit requirements; ZT2's fame stars on the Gate).

Give the first film a scenario-style finish line stated in one sentence (RCT's Forest Frontiers: '250 guests and 600 rating by October, Year 1'): 'Premiere your first picture by [date], with audience score N' — a real target inside the real economy, not a sandboxed tutorial.

Every link in the chain is a place with bodies: the audition is a physical queue of candidates outside Development & Casting (RCT's queue path as diegetic demand meter; The Movies' gate queue); rehearsal is the cast visibly on the stage with sides; shooting is a watchable spectacle — lights, dolly, slate-clap per scene (TPH's cure-machine lesson: spectacle teaches which building does what AND is the reward for a correct greenlight).

Rehearsal is the test mode (RCT's empty-train test run): before the shooting budget is fully committed, the rehearsal phase populates predicted quality readings on the production's dossier, and problems surface visibly on the lot. The player learns to read the film before betting on it.

The path runs on the real systems — real weekly tick, real cash, real audition scores, real phase engine. No fake tutorial state: guidance layer A watches the same deterministic state the engine produces, so the golden path is just the first traversal of the actual game, excellently staged.

End the first film with the full reward-and-diagnosis loop: a premiere event at the Gate (crowd density as the box-office chart, RCT's entrance-choke-point lesson), then a review screen where every line hovers to its cause in the player's own package decisions (The Movies' traceable reviews) — teaching film #2 in the act of scoring film #1.

Blocked-state discipline throughout: at every point on the path, if the player stalls, exactly one imperative line names the place and verb to unstick them, and the idle person stands visibly at the blocked building (fixing RCT's silent-dependency failure).

attention_pattern_library: Guiding Streams (The Movies): a sparkling trail from held object to the most sensible drop target, explicitly ignorable, with Tab jumping to the highest-priority stream and streams highlighting missing buildings in the Build menu. Works when the player has something 'in hand' and the next step is spatial; fails if multiple streams compete.

Imperative stage-completion bubbles (The Movies): 'Your script is complete and ready for casting in the Casting Office' — one sentence naming building + verb at every phase transition. Works for hand-off moments in a pipeline; the single best phrasing model for guidance text.

Priority-sorted info bubbles with threshold ticks (The Movies): hover any entity, highest-priority info first, bars with visible min/max thresholds, red '!' vs blue 'i' severity, click to burst, player-adjustable help level. Works at small scale; documented to drown the screen at large scale — must be rate-limited.
Pips / delta feed (The Movies): small transient icons on any stat change, green positive / red negative. Works as low-cost ambient awareness of drift; noise if every change fires one.

PA/radio ambient announcer (The Movies KMVS, Two Point Hospital tannoy): audible in-fiction voice reporting problems and foreshadowing era shifts, adjustable in options. Works as flavor-carrying telemetry that requires no click; fails when it becomes instruction or never shuts up (Planet Zoo narrators).

Token icon morph (The Movies): the movie card's icon changes script -> camera -> film can -> pulsing $, always matching physical location. Works as a zero-text pipeline progress readout; the icon itself tells you which building accepts it next.

Timeline strip with future-event icons (The Movies): hoverable icons for upcoming awards, research completions, taste shifts, retirements. Works for scheduled-future awareness (contract expiries, release dates) that ticker events would arrive too late for.

Red-line diagnosis in requirement lists (The Movies): the movie bubble lists required sets, entries turn red for missing/broken/occupied. Works whenever a plan has enumerable prerequisites; pairs with click-to-fix.

Emoticon/state glyphs worn on bodies (Zoo Tycoon smiley/frowny; TPH illnesses-as-costumes): individual state visible at full zoom-out, on the body, before any panel. Works for per-person mood/phase; the cheapest possible legibility layer.
Color-coded need meters with severity bands (Zoo Tycoon 1/2): green/yellow/red fills; a red need fires a message. Works when meters live on same-shaped cards so learning one card teaches all.

Named subject + place + problem alert grammar (Zoo Tycoon: 'Snow Leopard 1 has escaped into Exhibit 1'): text alerts, panels, and map share one namespace. Works always; the baseline for all message copy.
Aggregated chorus messages (Zoo Tycoon: 'Guests are complaining your zoo is too dirty'): the crowd speaks once when a pattern emerges. Works to prevent per-entity spam; essential at scale.

Pull-based advisor (Zoo Tycoon zookeeper recommendations): the player asks, the world answers as a shopping list in buy-menu vocabulary. Works because it keeps the push channel clean for genuine events and makes the player the diagnostician; fails if advisor text contradicts the meters (the camel case).

Live requirement bars during building/assembly (Zoo Tycoon suitability; Planet Zoo habitat bars): validation updates in real time while the player edits. Works to teach hidden formulas kinesthetically — watching the needle move IS the lesson.

News ticker with click-to-jump and archive (RCT; Anno; Frostpunk): every event is icon + sound + address; clicking pans to the subject. Works as the attention spine of the whole game; the notification is a teleport (for us: a pan), never just a paragraph.

Guest/individual thoughts as distributed telemetry (RCT 'I'm not paying that much!'; Planet Coaster): feedback attached to visible individuals, aggregated per-object in a tab. Works to deliver price/quality signals in-fiction; fails when the aggregate view is buried (RCT's mispricing problem) or the explanation is wrong (Planet Coaster's false 'couldn't find a way to ride').

Traffic-light state control on the object (RCT open/test/closed): a three-state control that is both status display and verb. Works for any object with a lifecycle the player gates (our develop/rehearse/shoot).
Physical queues as demand meters (RCT queue paths; The Movies gate queue): the line's length IS the KPI. Works for any demand/supply readout that can be embodied — auditions, premieres, hiring.

Animation-as-alarm / diegetic degradation (RCT stalled trains, vomit trails; ZT poop piles; Parkitect out-of-stock signs; TPH corridor queues; Frostpunk graves): the lot looks wrong before any number does. Works as the pre-textual alarm layer; requires believable agent behavior or it backfires.
Consequence as spectacle at the thing you built (RCT crashes; TPH cure machines): disasters and rewards happen visibly at their building. Works to teach cost and function faster than any number.

Status icons floating over buildings (Anno 1800): missing-input, no-workforce, storage-full, paused — each stall names its cause at the building. Works for standing state on a weekly tick; the direct model for milestone B level 2.
Upgrade arrow / available-verb beacon (Anno residences): a glow that says 'next step available here.' Works to make buildings advertise verbs; our klieg light on a greenlightable package.
Radius/coverage previews at placement (Planet Coaster; Frostpunk steam hubs; Anno markets): the game answers 'will this reach?' before commitment. Works for any placement with a spatial effect.

Opt-in overlay lenses (RCT/The Movies L-key attractiveness; Planet Zoo welfare view): one key repaints the lot by one metric. Works as opt-in only; auto-popping overlays broke trust (Planet Zoo complaints).

Persistent objective checklist (Two Point Hospital star objectives; RCT scenario goals): an always-visible list that ticks live and gates progression. Works as the tutorial-replacement backbone; the model for milestone A.

Cards as second handles on world objects (The Movies star/movie cards; RCT ride list): HUD elements jump-to and drag-from the actual lot entity, so panel-learning and lot-learning are the same learning. Works always; the rule that keeps panels from re-hiding the chain.

Ledger backstop (Anno's patched-in statistics screen): one aggregate screen answering 'how is the studio doing overall,' because world legibility answers only 'what is stuck here.' Works as a single Administration screen; its absence forced Ubisoft to patch one in.
Always-visible status strip (RCT cash/guests/rating/date): the scenario-relevant numbers never more than a glance away. Works for the 3-4 numbers the current goal depends on.
first_session_design: Minute 0-2, the establishing pan: the game opens with a slow camera pan across the small starting lot — Gate with a few hopefuls milling, Development & Casting lit, one dark soundstage — ending at Development & Casting, where a courier is visibly delivering a bound screenplay (The Movies' free-script-at-the-gates trick, staged as ZT2's crate-arrival). The persistent guidance checklist (milestone A) is already on screen with one active step: 'A screenplay has arrived — review it at Development & Casting.' The ticker prints the same line; clicking either pans (never teleports) to the building. Minute 2-5, first inspect and first verb: the player clicks Development & Casting; the roof lowers into the floorplan (milestone B level 3) showing the Readers' Room with the script binder sitting in it and the Packaging Table with four visibly empty slots (script/director/cast/budget — TPH's required-items starbursts). Reviewing the script is one click on the binder; its card teaches the universal card shape (title, genre, quality meter, one action button). Approving it fills the first package slot and the viability meter visibly ticks up — the live-needle lesson from Zoo Tycoon. Minute 5-9, auditions as a place: the checklist advances to 'Run auditions for your lead'; scheduling them spawns a physical queue of three candidates outside the building next tick (RCT queue as demand meter). The player clicks each candidate — same card shape, one audition verb — and casting the winner fills the cast slot on the Packaging Table while the rejected actors visibly walk back to the Gate. Director and budget follow the same grammar (one available director, a budget card at Administration reached by a guided pan). Minute 9-11, the greenlight: with all slots filled, the viability needle sits in the green, the Greenlight button becomes TPH's green checkmark, and Development & Casting sprouts a klieg-light beam (Anno's upgrade arrow). Greenlighting triggers the payoff spectacle: cast and crew assemble and physically walk across the lot to the soundstage — the single most important teaching image in the whole session (The Movies' procession), and the production token's icon morphs from binder to slate. Minute 11-15, the tick becomes legible: the player advances the first weekly ticks and watches phases as physical scenes — crew carrying flats from Scenery/Service during preproduction, the cast rehearsing with sides, then the first slate-clap of shooting under lights (the cure-machine reward). The soundstage's floating status icon reads 'SHOOTING — week 1 of 5,' the checklist shows the remaining arc (post, premiere) collapsed, and the ticker delivers its first flavor line through the PA. The session's contract is now proven: every step so far was a real engine action on real state; the player has learned the card grammar, the pan-to-subject rule, the package checklist, and the fact that progress is watched on the lot. The first film's premiere at the Gate — crowd density as box office, reviews hovering to causes — closes the loop in a later sitting, and film #2's checklist opens with the one step deliberately withheld here: 'Commission a screenplay.'
anti_patterns: Panel-completable actions the lot can't show (The Movies inverted, our current bug): the moment a management panel can do what no building shows, the chain goes invisible. Panels must be dossiers and second handles only.

Repeated identical manual drags with no delegation ramp (The Movies' star-nannying, relationship re-dragging, chasing stars out of the bar): any care/maintenance action performed a few times must become assignable policy, or the game becomes 'a chore rather than a pleasure.'

Alert flooding at scale (The Movies' bubble clutter; ZT2's message spam; Planet Zoo's alert triage homework): per-entity push notifications that don't aggregate into chorus messages drown the player exactly when they most need guidance.

Unexplainable derived numbers (ZT1's 0-star popularity wall; The Movies' opaque nine-factor quality formula): one number that refuses to decompose on click destroys trust in an otherwise legible game.

Silent spatial/logical dependencies (RCT's mechanic-can't-reach-the-exit loop): messaging the symptom ('still broken down') without the cause, forever. Every blocked state must name the blocking dependency and make it clickable.
Advisor text contradicting the meters (ZT's camel case): when the shopping-list advice and the numeric bars disagree, the player no longer knows which channel to believe.

Visible wrongness with invisible cause (TPH's queue dispatcher, Planet Coaster's false guest explanations): a world-as-interface game is uniquely damaged when agents behave illegibly or the world explains itself wrongly — worse than silence.
Chatty voiced hand-holding (Planet Zoo's career narrators, 'they never shut up'): voice-over cannot substitute for world legibility and gets muted and resented; voice is ambient telemetry only.
Auto-popping overlays (Planet Zoo's heatmap whiteout on placement): forced view modes break trust in the world view; overlays are opt-in lenses.

Tutorials that play themselves while the player watches (Planet Zoo career opener, 'like watching a YouTube video') or that teach too little and dump players on the wiki (Parkitect's depots and staff zones): the first session must be the player doing real actions on real state.
Menus-within-menus (Planet Coaster): verbs buried in nested menus instead of discovered at the moment of need in the world.
Two games taped together (The Movies' machinima seam): any layer whose output doesn't feed the economic loop suspends the tycoon momentum and alienates both audiences.
Gameable proxy metrics (The Movies' prestige tree-dotting): a lot-quality score not tied to named causal effects becomes stat-farming decoration.
No interesting failure (The Movies: impossible to have a disastrous shoot): a pipeline whose productions never fail interestingly flattens greenlighting into bigger-is-better churn.
Teleporting the camera on every notification: donors jump-cut; our ruling is pans — teleports skip the geography learning that makes the lot self-teaching.
Fake tutorial state: scripted onboarding flags divorced from engine state (versus RCT scenarios and TPH Hogsport, which run on the real sim) means the golden path teaches a game that doesn't exist.
ranked_recommendations: 1. Make the film ONE named, followable physical token whose icon morphs per phase and which renders at its current phase's building every tick, with phase transitions staged as watchable processions (cast walking to the stage, courier carrying the draft, cans carried to post). This is The Movies' core teaching device and RCT's ride-object pattern combined — the single highest-leverage fix for 'the chain is hidden in panels.' (Milestone C)

2. Ship the persistent state-derived guidance checklist whose steps are the filmmaking chain, each written as building + imperative verb, each ticking only when its physical consequence appears on the lot, each clickable to pan there — TPH's star objectives fused with The Movies' bubble voice. (Milestone A)

3. Turn the greenlight package into TPH's required-items checklist made physical: a Packaging Table inside Development & Casting with visibly empty script/director/cast/budget slots, a live viability needle that moves as slots fill (ZT's suitability bar), and a Greenlight button that stays disabled with the missing slot named. The player can never wonder why they can't greenlight. (Milestones B+C)

4. Open buildings into floorplans-as-verb-menus (The Movies' lowered walls): four inspection levels — hover card, floating Anno status icon naming any stall's cause, floorplan with lit/grayed verbs, tabbed RCT-style dossier — with every panel row a pan-link back into the world. (Milestone B)

5. Enforce blocked-state discipline everywhere: every stall names its blocking dependency in subject + place + problem grammar ('DESERT SERENADE stalled in Rehearsal — no leading lady, Stage 2'), clickable to pan, with the idle person visibly standing at the blocked building. This fixes RCT's and TPH's most-hated failure and is cheap on a deterministic engine. (Milestones A+D)

6. Start the first session with a commissioned screenplay already delivered (The Movies' free script at the gates) and a structurally tiny decision space (one director, three candidates, one stage — ZT's starter list), so session one completes review -> audition -> package -> greenlight -> shoot on real systems, and commissioning becomes film #2's first lesson. (Milestone E)

7. Build the trade-paper ticker as the attention spine: every event is icon + sound + lot address, click pans there, archive retained; standing state lives on building icons, individual state on worn body glyphs; chorus messages aggregate patterns; hard caps prevent The Movies' bubble flood. (Milestone D)

8. Make auditions, premieres, and hiring physical queues (RCT's queue path, The Movies' gate line): the line's length is the diegetic KPI, candidates walk from the Gate, rejected actors walk back — demand and draw are read by looking. (Milestones C+E)

9. Add the pull-based fixer/UPM advisor (ZT's zookeeper recommendations): one button that converts studio state into a shopping list in the exact strings the buildings use as verb labels, so a lost player's 'how do I make a movie?' is always answerable in one click without push-nagging. (Milestone A)

10. Make every judgment decompose: review lines and box-office results hover to named package causes (The Movies' traceable critic comments), rehearsal serves as RCT's test mode surfacing predicted quality before full commitment, and one Administration ledger screen backstops the world view (Anno's patched-in statistics lesson). Never ship an unexplainable number. (Milestones D+E)
